attributes.residual:
BEST RETAINED: real 628, insns T857/O855, multiset 6t = target-only +2 b +1 li +1 mr, ours-only -2 addi. Down from real 885 / 11t.

MECHANISM A, RESOLVED AND NAMED (this run's main finding). The target's `clrlwi. r0,r0,24` after `lbz r0,N(r1)` is NOT a redundant mask: peephole FUSES a separate `clrlwi` + `cmplwi` pair into the single recording `clrlwi.`. Proof, measured: with `#pragma peephole off` OUR build emitted 18 extra plain `clrlwi` AND kept the `cmplwi`s (probe 3), i.e. the fused form decomposes exactly. So a target `clrlwi.` means the u8 value was masked because it lived in a REGISTER WEB (MWCC cannot prove a register narrow), and the `lbz` in front of it is a SPILL RELOAD inserted after mask selection. Our `volatile` forced a true memory variable, so the front end emitted load-then-test and elided the mask entirely. Removing `volatile` restores the register web. Corroborating evidence in the same function: the two ALREADY-MATCHING sites at target 0x448 and 0x778 are `clrlwi. r0,r20,24` / `clrlwi. r0,r24,24` on plain (non-volatile) u8 locals held in registers.

MECHANISM B, STILL OPEN: target-only +2 b at 0x9d4/0x9d8, the CARDDelete switch. Target emits `b ->9dc` followed by an UNREACHABLE `b ->6c`; we emit neither and fall straight through. Decoded: `b ->9dc` is the case-body edge and `b ->6c` is the per-leaf default edge that MWCC's decision-tree generator always emits; our build removes the dead one and then the survivor becomes a branch-to-next and is removed too. Global peephole off is REFUTED as the lever (probe 3, catastrophic), and `opt_dead_code` is not a pragma MWCC honours here (probe 5, folded). Run-26 already killed case-order reordering. NOTE THE POPULATION: the identical `bne X / b Y` goto-pair signature also appears in get_vmu_directory at 0x48 and writeGauntletSave at 0xe4 -- three functions in this one TU. This is a TU-LEVEL flag/pragma question, not a per-function source-shape question, and the next agent should treat it as one (census first).

MECHANISM C, STILL OPEN: ~15 identical schedule clusters, each a single `li rX,C` displaced by ONE position across a following store, with every other word and register in the block identical. Representative, target 0x140: `li r14,0 / stw r14,@lbl_80344A24 / li r0,-1 / stw r0,@lbl_80344A18`; ours: `li r14,0 / li r0,-1 / stw r14,@lbl_80344A24 / stw r0,@lbl_80344A18`. Our build hoists the `li` one slot earlier. Per claim.law.C1 step 0 this IS a legal permutation in our colouring (the displaced `li` defines r0; the crossed `stw` neither reads nor writes r0), so it is a WebFrank instruction_permutation MEMBER, but it needs ~15 windows.

MECHANISM D, STILL OPEN, and the run-26 record did not know about it: the STACK SLOT LAYOUT is systematically wrong. Measured census of every differing (r1) row: our four `volatile` scaffold words (bigSize, dirTab, opts, removedCb) sit at the BOTTOM of the local block (ours 148/152/156/160) while the target has them at the TOP (target 168/172/176/180), and every non-volatile local is correspondingly +16 in ours (checkMsg 148->164, serial 156->172, const temp 164->180, flag group 152-154 -> 168-170, flag group 160-162 -> 176-178). CRITICALLY, the RELATIVE order inside the non-volatile sub-block is ALREADY CORRECT on both sides (ascending: checkMsg, found-group, serial, keepPair-group, const). So this is not a declaration-order defect that claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order can fix -- it is that MWCC segregates `volatile` locals into their own sub-block and places it BELOW the non-volatile one, whereas the target has no such segregation. Removing volatile from the four is measured NEGATIVE (probe 4). The open question for the next agent is how to keep those four memory-homed WITHOUT the volatile qualifier.
